title: From Growth to Visibility: Bureaucratic Incentives After China's Cadre Evaluation Reforms
gist: Xi Jinping's cadre evaluation reforms de-emphasized GDP but, combined with tighter fiscal and administrative constraints, redirected Chinese local-official competition from growth maximization toward performative, highly visible spotlight projects (亮点工程) engineered for upward political signaling. Field interviews in Shanghai and Guangxi show these projects are often substantively hollow yet career-rewarding, and Xi's 2026 correct view on political achievement campaign attacks the symptom (individual cadre morality) rather than the structural incentive that produces it.

insights.claim: Xi Jinping's reduction of GDP weighting in China's cadre evaluation system did not eliminate performative local governance but converted it into competition over politically visible success stories aimed at higher-level leaders.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Chinese local-government capital allocation is increasingly driven by signaling value rather than return on investment, degrading the informational content of provincial-level project announcements used as China growth inputs.
